items.title: Limited Access to OCI Generative AI Models with IAM Policies
items.content:
The `target.model.id` condition allows to limit, by means of IAM policies, what models of Generative AI can be used by a group. Policies can allow ids of specific models, allow ids that match a pattern or exclude ids and specified patterns.

To restrict access from the console, give the group permission `inspect generative-ai-model` so that its members can list and select models. He later grants the group permission `use generative-ai-family` with a `target.model.id` condition to restrict the models they can invoke. The permission to list models does not allow models to be invoked outside that condition.

Although policy examples use resource added type `generative-ai-family`, `target.model.id` applies only to inference using `generative-ai-chat`, `generative-ai-text-embedding` and `generative-ai-text-rerank`. Do not restrict models management operations of other family resource types.

For more information and policy examples, please consult Limited Access to Models with IAM Policies.

items.title: Add AI Guardrails to Dedicated AI Cluster's OCI Generative AI Endpoints
items.content:
OCI Generative AI allows AI scanners to be enabled for content restraint (CM), prompt injection (PI) and personal identification information (pII) at endpoints housed at Dedicated AI Cluster. Chat and text embedding endpoints are supported in commercial regions and the feature is available at Console and using API, SDK and CLI.

The ranger can be added by creating or updating a endpoint. In Inform mode, the inference runs and the response includes the guarrail results for review. In Block mode, an attempt was made to reject requests when violations were found. an example response is `HTTP 400: Inappropriate content detected!`. The rails are applied in real time as part of the inference of endpoint.

The contents moderation and prompt injection rangers were evaluated with multilingual reference datasets. The actual performance can vary depending on the languages, domains, data distributions and usage patterns that are present in the data provided by customers. OCI does not guarantee identical performance features for all actual deployments.

The content restraint capacity was evaluated with RTPLX, a public multilingual assessment package that includes more than 38 languages. The results should be interpreted with care.

items.title: Add Image Moderation to OCI Generative AI Guarding
items.content:
OCI Generative AI allows moderate images by API `ApplyGuardrails`using existing content restraint capacity. The feature is available with Guarrails system version `1.1.0` and helps to identify unsafe content in independent or requests multimodal models that combine text and images. It can be used to evaluate user uploaded images, generated images, screen capture and embedded text images.

To use it, request have to include `multimodalInput` with an item with a value `type` be `IMAGE`, enabling `contentModerationConfig` and specify the version `1.1.0` with `guardrailVersionConfig`. JPEG, PNG and WebP images are supported. One request can include up to five images, up to 170 Megamapixthem each.

The inputs from image are subject to limitation by tokens of image with a preset limit of 200,000 tokens of image A minute. If a higher limit is required, an increase in the service limit may be requested.

The results are returned within the result `contentModeration` existing, including score `OVERALL`; No separate response item shall be added. The field `flaggedModalities` indicates how they contributed to the result and conforms to the values `TEXT` e `IMAGE`. In the example, `OVERALL` have a score of `1.0` and `flaggedModalities` contains `TEXT` e `IMAGE`.

The content moderation was evaluated with RTPLX, a public set of multilingual assessment that cover more than 38 languages. The performance observed at RTPLX may be ungeneralised to all contexts, domains, dialects or actual use patterns. Performance can also vary by languages, domains, data distributions and data use patterns provided by customers. OCI does not guarantee identical performance characteristics at all deployments Realty.

items.title: Add Security Modes to Cohere Models at OCI Generative AI
items.content:
OCI Generative AI allows an optional security mode to be added to Cohere models during a chat session. The parameter adds a safety instruction to the responses generated by the model.

Strict aims to avoid sensitive issues, such as violent or sexual acts and Soez language, and aims to offer a safer experience by prohibiting responses or recommendations that it considers inappropriate. It's intended for corporate uses, such as corporate communications and customer care.

The Contextual mode lays down less restrictions than Strict and maintains basic protections aimed at rejecting harmful or illegal suggestions. It allows Soez language, some toxic content, sexually explicit and violent content and medical, financial or legal information. It's designed for entertainment, creative or academic uses. The feature is only available for `cohere.command-r-08-2024`, `cohere.command-r-plus-08-2024` and Cohere models launched after them.

items.title: Background Mode Available for OCI Responses API
items.content:
The OCI Responses API supports `background mode` for requests that could take more than the application wants to keep the original connection open. The processing continues asynchronous and the application can be consulted with the state and the result with the response ID.

To run an asynchronous request, set `background` into `true` by creating an answer. The request can continue to run after the initial call back to the API. You can recover your answer for your ID while your state is `queued` or `in_progress`. When processing is complete, you can get an output or check with the final state. You can also cancel a background response that isn't finished.

To transmit events and preserve the possibility of reconnecting, create an answer with `background=true` and `stream=true`. If stream stops, repeat after the last event received with your `sequence_number`.

items.title: Receive Notifications about Model Retirement Dates in OCI Generative AI
items.content:
OCI Generative AI incorporated messages into the console, date parameters at the API and OCI ads to report about obsolescence and model retirement. The Console shows warning messages for old models.

After a model becomes obsolete, each call inference to that model includes the `model-retirement-info` response header, indicating its next retirement date. Once that date passed, calls inference to API for the retired model stop functioning.

The API `GetModel` allows to check detailed dates of obsolescence and retirement using `timeDeprecated`, `timeOnDemandRetired` and `timeDedicatedRetired`. These fields indicate, respectively, when the model becomes obsolete and when it is withdrawn for the on-demand and dedicated modes.

When subscribing to the OCI Notifications service, messages about obsolescence and model retirement are received. For on-demand mode, 14 and 7 are sent days before retirement date. for dedicated mode, 90, 60, 30 and 7 earlier days. Subscription to OCI Announcements allows to receive service notifications. The instructions are at Subkirbing to Announcements.

items.title: OCI Generative AI Now Admit To Guards at low demand mode
items.content:
OCI Generative AI allows AI scanners to be enabled for content restraint (CM), prompts (PI) injection and personal information that can be identified (pII). The feature is available using API for chat and text embedding models at demand in commercial regions.

The aim of moderation of content is to classify harmful content in prompts and responses, such as hate speech, harassment, violence and explicit material, through an internal model. It includes binary categories `OVERALL` (unsafe) and `BLOCKLIST` (preset words).

The prompts injection defence aims at detecting malicious instructions in prompts and embedded contexts, for example, document-hidden instructions, to help prevent unauthorized overlays. Reforms a binary risk score: `0.0` for insurance and `1.0` for risky. The aim of pII detection is to identify sensitive data, such as names (`PERSON`), e-mails (`EMAIL`) and phone numbers (`TELEPHONE_NUMBER`). The results can include the text found, its label, its location (`offset` and `length`) and a confidence score.

The API `ApplyGuardrails` allows us to evaluate real-time inputs with inference without `endpoints`. It applies to all chat and embedding models that OCI Generative AI offers in commercial regions. Returns detailed results, such as restraint categories, pII and PI score for its programme management. doesn't block by default.

The content moderation capabilities were evaluated with RTPLX, a public multilingual comparative assessment dataset covering more than 38 languages. The performance observed at RTPLX may not fully generalize all actual contexts, domains, dialects or patterns of use. The actual performance can also vary with the languages, domains, data distributions and usage patterns currently available in the data provided by customers. OCI does not guarantee identical performance features for all actual deployments.

cover.alt: OCI Generative AI Now Admit To Guards at low demand mode

items.title: Set A Storage Version at OCI Generative AI
items.content:
OCI Generative AI allows you to select a specific version of Guardrails by using API `ApplyGuardrails`. The versions follow the semantic versioner scheme, such as `1.0.0`, and represent the conduct of protection for content restraint (CM), prompts (PI) injection and identification of personal information (pII).

Setting up a version allows stable behaviour to be maintained. The version configuration can also be omitted to use the default version. Before to choose from, `ListGuardrailVersions` allows to check available versions, its state of the life cycle - for example, activated, obsolete or withdrawn - and, as appropriate, the date of activation, obsolescence or withdrawal. To use a specific version, `guardrailVersionConfig` will be added to request `ApplyGuardrailsDetails`.

The `1.0.0` version is the initial version of AI Guarrails and includes fundamental safety checks for CM, PI and pII. The `1.0.1` version improves the accuracy of CM and PI.

The protections of CM and PI have been evaluated with multilingual reference datasets. The actual performance may vary with the languages, domains, data distribution and usage patterns that are present in the data provided by customers. OCI does not guarantee an identical performance for all actual deployments. The content restraint capabilities were also evaluated with RTPLX, a widely available multilingual reference set that includes more than 38 languages. The results should be interpreted with caution as the content generated by AI may contain errors or omissions.

Combining text and image can jointly represent related textual and visual context, as a product image with its description, an explanatory text graph or a image document with its surrounding content.
